This is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas.

Muhammad ibn Na'im informed us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Aziz informed us: al-Qasim ibn Salam informed us: Haytham related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he read it *'Ibadu al-Rahman*.

Sa'id said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "In my codex it is *'Abd al-Rahman*." He said: "Erase it and write *'Ibad al-Rahman*." The confirmation of this reading is His saying: ﴿Rather, they are honored servants﴾ [[Surah al-Anbiya': 26.]]. The others read *'inda al-Rahman* with a *nun*, and Abu Hatim chose this, saying: Because this is praise, whereas when you say *'Ibad al-Rahman* [servants of the Most Merciful], its confirmation is His saying, ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ [[Surah al-A'raf: 206.]].

﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾: did they attend their creation, so that they would know that they are females? The people of Medina read *ushhidu* in the passive voice, meaning "were they made to witness." *Khalqahum*: at the time they were created. ﴿Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned﴾: that the angels are daughters of Allah.

﴿And they say: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them"﴾: meaning the angels, according to Qatada, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi. Mujahid said: it means the idols. They are only guessing﴾, meaning lying.

It was said it means blessing. 'Adi ibn Zayd said: "After prosperity, dominion, and blessing (*al-umma*), and We showed them the graves there." It was also said that the two are dialects with one meaning.

*Qal* [he said]: the common reading is in the imperative. Ibn 'Amir read it in the declarative, and Hafs ibn 'Asim related the same.

﴿"Even if I brought you better guidance than that which you found your fathers upon?"﴾: Abu Ja'far read *awa-law ja'akum* with an *alif* [as a question]. The rest read *ji'tukum* in the singular. *Bi-ahda*: with a more correct religion. ﴿They said: "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent." So We took retribution upon them. Then observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾

﴿And [mention] when Abraham said to his father and his people: "Indeed, I am free (*bara'*) from what you worship"﴾: *bara'* means "free"; it is not dualized, pluralized, or feminized, because it is a verbal noun placed in the position of an adjective. In the reading of Abdullah it is *bari'*, with a *ya'*. ﴿Except for He who created me, for He will guide me﴾: created me; the meaning of the verse is: "I am free from every deity except He who created me, for He will guide me to His religion."

﴿And He made it (*wa-ja'alaha*), referring to this statement and word, a word that remains among his descendants﴾: Mujahid and Qatada said: it means *la ilaha illa Allah* [there is no god but Allah]. Al-Qurazi said: it means the will of Abraham that he enjoined upon his sons, which remains in his progeny and offspring, and which Allah mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah: ﴿And Abraham instructed his sons with it﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 132.]]. Ibn Zayd said: it means his saying: ﴿I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 131.]], and he recited ﴿He named you "the Muslims"﴾ [[Surah al-Hajj: 78.]].

﴿So that they may return﴾ from their disbelief to obedience, and repent. ﴿But I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers﴾ in this world, so I did not destroy them, nor hasten punishment upon them for their disbelief. ﴿Until there came to them the truth﴾: the Qur'an. Al-Dahhak said: Islam. ﴿And a clear messenger﴾: who clarifies for them the signs and the rulings, and he is Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And when the truth came to them, the Qur'an, they said: "This is magic, and we disbelieve in it."﴾ ﴿And they said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two towns?"﴾ That is, from one of the two towns. They did not differ that the two towns are Mecca and al-Ta'if, but they differed about who the two men were. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira from Mecca, who was called the "basil of Quraysh," and Habib ibn 'Amr ibn 'Umayr al-Thaqafi from al-Ta'if.

Mujahid said: 'Utba ibn al-Rabi'a from Mecca, and Ibn 'Abd Yalil al-Thaqafi from al-Ta'if. Qatada said: they are al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi and Abu Mas'ud 'Urwa ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. Al-Suddi said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Kinana ibn 'Abd 'Amr ibn 'Umayr.

Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Yahya read *ma'ayishahum* [their livelihoods]. ﴿And We raised some of them above others in degrees, that some of them may take others in service (*sukhriyyan*)﴾: that the wealthy may employ the poor laborers with their wealth through work, and that they may use them, so that some become a means of livelihood for others in this world: this one with his wealth, and that one with his work. This is the saying of al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. Qatada and al-Dahhak said: meaning that some own others, so this one is the slave of that one. It was said: some mock others. It was said: some subjugate others.

﴿And the mercy of your Lord﴾: meaning Paradise, ﴿is better than what they accumulate﴾ of wealth in this world. ﴿And if not that the people would become one community﴾: united in disbelief, so they would all become disbelievers. This is the saying of most exegetes. Ibn Zayd said: meaning: ﴿and if not that the people would become one community﴾ in pursuit of the world and preferring it over the Hereafter.

﴿We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses, roofs of silver﴾: Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Humayd, and Yahya ibn Wathhab read *saqfan* with a *fatha* on the *sin*, in the singular, meaning the plural, by analogy with His saying: ﴿So the roof fell upon them from above them﴾ [[Surah al-Nahl: 26.]]. Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi read *ma'arij*, and both are dialects; the singular is *mi'raj*, like *maftah* and *mafatih*.

"Our glory and splendor have reached the heavens, and we hope for a height beyond that."

That is, an ascent.

﴿And for their houses, doors of silver, and couches of silver upon which they recline, and ornamentation﴾: meaning, We would also have given them, besides that, ornamentation, which is gold, like the phrase "a decorated house." It may be that the meaning is "silver and ornamentation," and when the preposition is removed it becomes accusative.

﴿Or one who is brought up in ornaments﴾: the people of Kufa read *yunashsha'u* with a *damma* on the *ya'*, a *fatha* on the *nun*, and a *shadda* on the *shin*, in the passive voice, meaning "one who is raised by others." Others read *yanshu'u* with a *fatha* on the *ya'*, a *jazm* on the *nun*, and a lightened *shin*, meaning "grows up and becomes great."

﴿In the ornament﴾: in adornment, meaning women. Mujahid said: He permitted women silk and gold, and he recited this verse.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Za'farani informed us: Yahya ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib related to us: Muhammad ibn Ubayd related to us: Ubaydullah ibn Umar related to us, from Nafi', from Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Gold and silk are forbidden to the males of my community and lawful to its females" [193] [[Fath al-Bari: 10/250; Muntakhab Musnad 'Abd ibn Humayd: 193.]].

﴿And he is not clear in dispute﴾: lacking clarity of argument, due to their weakness and foolishness. Qatada said regarding this verse: A woman seldom speaks with her argument without the argument turning against her. In the Codex of Abdullah (*wa-huwa fi al-kalam ghayr mubin*) [and he is not clear in speech].

Some exegetes said: This verse refers to their idols which they worshipped, honored, and adorned, though they do not speak or utter a sound. Ibn Zayd said: These are their images which they make of silver and gold, and they adorn them and worship them.

This is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas.

Muhammad ibn Na'im informed us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Aziz informed us: al-Qasim ibn Salam informed us: Haytham related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he read it *'Ibadu al-Rahman*.

Sa'id said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "In my codex it is *'Abd al-Rahman*." He said: "Erase it and write *'Ibad al-Rahman*." The confirmation of this reading is His saying: ﴿Rather, they are honored servants﴾ [[Surah al-Anbiya': 26.]]. The others read *'inda al-Rahman* with a *nun*, and Abu Hatim chose this, saying: Because this is praise, whereas when you say *'Ibad al-Rahman* [servants of the Most Merciful], its confirmation is His saying, ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ [[Surah al-A'raf: 206.]].

﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾: did they attend their creation, so that they would know that they are females? The people of Medina read *ushhidu* in the passive voice, meaning "were they made to witness." *Khalqahum*: at the time they were created. ﴿Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned﴾: that the angels are daughters of Allah.

﴿And they say: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them"﴾: meaning the angels, according to Qatada, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi. Mujahid said: it means the idols. They are only guessing﴾, meaning lying.

It was said it means blessing. 'Adi ibn Zayd said: "After prosperity, dominion, and blessing (*al-umma*), and We showed them the graves there." It was also said that the two are dialects with one meaning.

*Qal* [he said]: the common reading is in the imperative. Ibn 'Amir read it in the declarative, and Hafs ibn 'Asim related the same.

﴿"Even if I brought you better guidance than that which you found your fathers upon?"﴾: Abu Ja'far read *awa-law ja'akum* with an *alif* [as a question]. The rest read *ji'tukum* in the singular. *Bi-ahda*: with a more correct religion. ﴿They said: "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent." So We took retribution upon them. Then observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾

﴿And [mention] when Abraham said to his father and his people: "Indeed, I am free (*bara'*) from what you worship"﴾: *bara'* means "free"; it is not dualized, pluralized, or feminized, because it is a verbal noun placed in the position of an adjective. In the reading of Abdullah it is *bari'*, with a *ya'*. ﴿Except for He who created me, for He will guide me﴾: created me; the meaning of the verse is: "I am free from every deity except He who created me, for He will guide me to His religion."

﴿And He made it (*wa-ja'alaha*), referring to this statement and word, a word that remains among his descendants﴾: Mujahid and Qatada said: it means *la ilaha illa Allah* [there is no god but Allah]. Al-Qurazi said: it means the will of Abraham that he enjoined upon his sons, which remains in his progeny and offspring, and which Allah mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah: ﴿And Abraham instructed his sons with it﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 132.]]. Ibn Zayd said: it means his saying: ﴿I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 131.]], and he recited ﴿He named you "the Muslims"﴾ [[Surah al-Hajj: 78.]].

﴿So that they may return﴾ from their disbelief to obedience, and repent. ﴿But I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers﴾ in this world, so I did not destroy them, nor hasten punishment upon them for their disbelief. ﴿Until there came to them the truth﴾: the Qur'an. Al-Dahhak said: Islam. ﴿And a clear messenger﴾: who clarifies for them the signs and the rulings, and he is Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And when the truth came to them, the Qur'an, they said: "This is magic, and we disbelieve in it."﴾ ﴿And they said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two towns?"﴾ That is, from one of the two towns. They did not differ that the two towns are Mecca and al-Ta'if, but they differed about who the two men were. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira from Mecca, who was called the "basil of Quraysh," and Habib ibn 'Amr ibn 'Umayr al-Thaqafi from al-Ta'if.

Mujahid said: 'Utba ibn al-Rabi'a from Mecca, and Ibn 'Abd Yalil al-Thaqafi from al-Ta'if. Qatada said: they are al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi and Abu Mas'ud 'Urwa ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. Al-Suddi said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Kinana ibn 'Abd 'Amr ibn 'Umayr.

Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Yahya read *ma'ayishahum* [their livelihoods]. ﴿And We raised some of them above others in degrees, that some of them may take others in service (*sukhriyyan*)﴾: that the wealthy may employ the poor laborers with their wealth through work, and that they may use them, so that some become a means of livelihood for others in this world: this one with his wealth, and that one with his work. This is the saying of al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. Qatada and al-Dahhak said: meaning that some own others, so this one is the slave of that one. It was said: some mock others. It was said: some subjugate others.

﴿And the mercy of your Lord﴾: meaning Paradise, ﴿is better than what they accumulate﴾ of wealth in this world. ﴿And if not that the people would become one community﴾: united in disbelief, so they would all become disbelievers. This is the saying of most exegetes. Ibn Zayd said: meaning: ﴿and if not that the people would become one community﴾ in pursuit of the world and preferring it over the Hereafter.

﴿We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses, roofs of silver﴾: Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Humayd, and Yahya ibn Wathhab read *saqfan* with a *fatha* on the *sin*, in the singular, meaning the plural, by analogy with His saying: ﴿So the roof fell upon them from above them﴾ [[Surah al-Nahl: 26.]]. Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi read *ma'arij*, and both are dialects; the singular is *mi'raj*, like *maftah* and *mafatih*.

"Our glory and splendor have reached the heavens, and we hope for a height beyond that."

That is, an ascent.

﴿And for their houses, doors of silver, and couches of silver upon which they recline, and ornamentation﴾: meaning, We would also have given them, besides that, ornamentation, which is gold, like the phrase "a decorated house." It may be that the meaning is "silver and ornamentation," and when the preposition is removed it becomes accusative.

﴿And all that is but the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾: Asim and Hamza read *lamma* with a *shadda* on the *mim* [meaning "all of it" as an emphatic], as in *wa-in kullu dhalika lamma mata'u al-hayat al-dunya*. The others lightened it, in the sense of *dhalika mata'u al-hayat al-dunya* [that is the enjoyment of the life of this world], so *lamma* is a linking particle. ﴿And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous﴾: for the believers.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us: Ahmad ibn Shadhan informed us: Jaghwayh ibn Muhammad informed us: Salih ibn Muhammad related to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Aban related to us, from Sulayman ibn al-Qays al-'Amiri, from Ka'b, who said: I find in some books: "Were it not that My believing servant would grieve, I would crown the head of the disbeliever with crowns; he would not be struck with a headache, nor would a vein throb with pain from him."

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah related to us: al-Firyabi related to us: Ibrahim ibn al-'Ala' al-Zubaydi related to us: Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash related to us, from Tha'laba ibn Muslim, from Muslim ibn Abi al-Mujarrad, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to say: "If a man were to flee from his provision, it would pursue him until it overtook him, just as death overtakes one who flees from it. Everyone has a term he will reach, a trace he will tread, a provision he will eat, and a trade by which he will earn. So fear Allah and be graceful in seeking. Let not the delay of some provision lead you to seek it through disobedience to Allah the Exalted, for what is with Him is not attained except through obeying Him, and what is with Him is not reached through disobeying Him. So fear Allah and be graceful in seeking."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 43, verses 16–35:**

﴿Or has He taken daughters from what He creates, and chosen sons for you?﴾ *Akhlasakum* (chosen you), *wa-khassasakum* (singled you out) with sons. Its parallel is His saying, ﴿Has your Lord then chosen sons for you and taken daughters from the angels?﴾ [[Surah al-Isra': 40.]]

﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful, his face becomes darkened, and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾: meaning daughters. Its evidence is in al-Nahl: ﴿his face becomes darkened, and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾, from sorrow and rage.

﴿Or one who is brought up in ornaments﴾: the people of Kufa read *yunashsha'u* with a *damma* on the *ya'*, a *fatha* on the *nun*, and a *shadda* on the *shin*, in the passive voice, meaning "one who is raised by others." Others read *yanshu'u* with a *fatha* on the *ya'*, a *jazm* on the *nun*, and a lightened *shin*, meaning "grows up and becomes great."

﴿In the ornament﴾: in adornment, meaning women. Mujahid said: He permitted women silk and gold, and he recited this verse.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Za'farani informed us: Yahya ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib related to us: Muhammad ibn Ubayd related to us: Ubaydullah ibn Umar related to us, from Nafi', from Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Gold and silk are forbidden to the males of my community and lawful to its females" [193] [[Fath al-Bari: 10/250; Muntakhab Musnad 'Abd ibn Humayd: 193.]].

﴿And he is not clear in dispute﴾: lacking clarity of argument, due to their weakness and foolishness. Qatada said regarding this verse: A woman seldom speaks with her argument without the argument turning against her. In the Codex of Abdullah (*wa-huwa fi al-kalam ghayr mubin*) [and he is not clear in speech].

Some exegetes said: This verse refers to their idols which they worshipped, honored, and adorned, though they do not speak or utter a sound. Ibn Zayd said: These are their images which they make of silver and gold, and they adorn them and worship them.

*Man* in *Awa-man yunashsha'u* has three possible grammatical positions (*wujuh*): the nominative (*raf'*) as the subject of a new sentence (*ibtida'*); the accusative (*nasb*) by an implied verb, whose sense is: "they make it a lord or daughters of Allah"; and the genitive (*khafd*), in response to His saying *mimma yakhluqu* [from what He creates] and His saying: *bima sarat* [by what they have become]...

﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾: Abu 'Amr and the people of Kufa read *'ibad al-Rahman* with an alif and a *ya'*, and Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading, saying: Because the attribution in it is higher, and because Allah only denied them in His saying "daughters of Allah," so He informed that they are His servants and not His daughters. This is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas.

Muhammad ibn Na'im informed us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Aziz informed us: al-Qasim ibn Salam informed us: Haytham related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he read it *'Ibadu al-Rahman*.

Sa'id said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "In my codex it is *'Abd al-Rahman*." He said: "Erase it and write *'Ibad al-Rahman*." The confirmation of this reading is His saying: ﴿Rather, they are honored servants﴾ [[Surah al-Anbiya': 26.]]. The others read *'inda al-Rahman* with a *nun*, and Abu Hatim chose this, saying: Because this is praise, whereas when you say *'Ibad al-Rahman* [servants of the Most Merciful], its confirmation is His saying, ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ [[Surah al-A'raf: 206.]].

﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾: did they attend their creation, so that they would know that they are females? The people of Medina read *ushhidu* in the passive voice, meaning "were they made to witness." *Khalqahum*: at the time they were created. ﴿Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned﴾: that the angels are daughters of Allah.

﴿And they say: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them"﴾: meaning the angels, according to Qatada, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi. Mujahid said: it means the idols. They said that Allah did not hasten punishment upon them for worshipping them, which indicates His approval of their worship. Allah said: ﴿They have no knowledge of that. They are only guessing﴾, meaning lying.

﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so they are holding fast to it?﴾: that is, before this Qur'an. ﴿Rather, they say: "We found our fathers upon a religion (*ummah*)", and we are guided by their footsteps.﴾ The common reading is *ummatin* with a *damma* on the *alif*, meaning religion and creed. 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz and Mujahid read *'immatin* with a *kasra* on the *alif*, and they differed on its meaning. It was said it means the path and the aim, from their saying *amamtu* [I aimed]. It was said it means blessing. 'Adi ibn Zayd said: "After prosperity, dominion, and blessing (*al-umma*), and We showed them the graves there." It was also said that the two are dialects with one meaning.

﴿And similarly, We did not send before you a warner to a town except that its affluent ones said: "We found our fathers upon a religion, and we are following in their footsteps."﴾: *mustanun* (following), *muttabi'un* (adhering).

*Qal* [he said]: the common reading is in the imperative. Ibn 'Amir read it in the declarative, and Hafs ibn 'Asim related the same.

﴿"Even if I brought you better guidance than that which you found your fathers upon?"﴾: Abu Ja'far read *awa-law ja'akum* with an *alif* [as a question]. The rest read *ji'tukum* in the singular. *Bi-ahda*: with a more correct religion. ﴿They said: "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent." So We took retribution upon them. Then observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾

﴿And [mention] when Abraham said to his father and his people: "Indeed, I am free (*bara'*) from what you worship"﴾: *bara'* means "free"; it is not dualized, pluralized, or feminized, because it is a verbal noun placed in the position of an adjective. In the reading of Abdullah it is *bari'*, with a *ya'*. ﴿Except for He who created me, for He will guide me﴾: created me; the meaning of the verse is: "I am free from every deity except He who created me, for He will guide me to His religion."

﴿And He made it (*wa-ja'alaha*), referring to this statement and word, a word that remains among his descendants﴾: Mujahid and Qatada said: it means *la ilaha illa Allah* [there is no god but Allah]. Al-Qurazi said: it means the will of Abraham that he enjoined upon his sons, which remains in his progeny and offspring, and which Allah mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah: ﴿And Abraham instructed his sons with it﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 132.]]. Ibn Zayd said: it means his saying: ﴿I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 131.]], and he recited ﴿He named you "the Muslims"﴾ [[Surah al-Hajj: 78.]].

﴿So that they may return﴾ from their disbelief to obedience, and repent. ﴿But I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers﴾ in this world, so I did not destroy them, nor hasten punishment upon them for their disbelief. ﴿Until there came to them the truth﴾: the Qur'an. Al-Dahhak said: Islam. ﴿And a clear messenger﴾: who clarifies for them the signs and the rulings, and he is Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And when the truth came to them, the Qur'an, they said: "This is magic, and we disbelieve in it."﴾ ﴿And they said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two towns?"﴾ That is, from one of the two towns. They did not differ that the two towns are Mecca and al-Ta'if, but they differed about who the two men were. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira from Mecca, who was called the "basil of Quraysh," and Habib ibn 'Amr ibn 'Umayr al-Thaqafi from al-Ta'if.

Mujahid said: 'Utba ibn al-Rabi'a from Mecca, and Ibn 'Abd Yalil al-Thaqafi from al-Ta'if. Qatada said: they are al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi and Abu Mas'ud 'Urwa ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. Al-Suddi said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Kinana ibn 'Abd 'Amr ibn 'Umayr.

Allah the Glorified and Exalted said: ﴿Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾: His prophethood and honor, so that they would give it to whomever they wish. ﴿We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world﴾: We made this one rich and that one poor, this one a king and that one a subject. Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Yahya read *ma'ayishahum* [their livelihoods]. ﴿And We raised some of them above others in degrees, that some of them may take others in service (*sukhriyyan*)﴾: that the wealthy may employ the poor laborers with their wealth through work, and that they may use them, so that some become a means of livelihood for others in this world: this one with his wealth, and that one with his work. This is the saying of al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. Qatada and al-Dahhak said: meaning that some own others, so this one is the slave of that one. It was said: some mock others. It was said: some subjugate others.

﴿And the mercy of your Lord﴾: meaning Paradise, ﴿is better than what they accumulate﴾ of wealth in this world. ﴿And if not that the people would become one community﴾: united in disbelief, so they would all become disbelievers. This is the saying of most exegetes. Ibn Zayd said: meaning: ﴿and if not that the people would become one community﴾ in pursuit of the world and preferring it over the Hereafter.

﴿We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses, roofs of silver﴾: Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Humayd, and Yahya ibn Wathhab read *saqfan* with a *fatha* on the *sin*, in the singular, meaning the plural, by analogy with His saying: ﴿So the roof fell upon them from above them﴾ [[Surah al-Nahl: 26.]]. The rest read *suqufan* with a *damma* on the *sin* and *qaf*, in the plural. It is said *saqf* and *saqqaf*, like *rahn* and *rahhan*. Abu 'Ubayd said: there is no third reading for them. It was said it is the plural of *saqif*, and it was said it is the plural of *suqf*, and the plural of the plural. ﴿And stairways﴾: that is, ascents, steps, and ladders. Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi read *ma'arij*, and both are dialects; the singular is *mi'raj*, like *maftah* and *mafatih*.

﴿Upon which they would ascend﴾: rise up, climb, and ascend by them. One says *zahartu 'ala al-sath* [I ascended upon the roof] when you climb it. Al-Nabigha al-Ja'di said:

"Our glory and splendor have reached the heavens, and we hope for a height beyond that."

That is, an ascent.

﴿And for their houses, doors of silver, and couches of silver upon which they recline, and ornamentation﴾: meaning, We would also have given them, besides that, ornamentation, which is gold, like the phrase "a decorated house." It may be that the meaning is "silver and ornamentation," and when the preposition is removed it becomes accusative.

﴿And all that is but the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾: Asim and Hamza read *lamma* with a *shadda* on the *mim* [meaning "all of it" as an emphatic], as in *wa-in kullu dhalika lamma mata'u al-hayat al-dunya*. The others lightened it, in the sense of *dhalika mata'u al-hayat al-dunya* [that is the enjoyment of the life of this world], so *lamma* is a linking particle. ﴿And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous﴾: for the believers.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us: Ahmad ibn Shadhan informed us: Jaghwayh ibn Muhammad informed us: Salih ibn Muhammad related to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Aban related to us, from Sulayman ibn al-Qays al-'Amiri, from Ka'b, who said: I find in some books: "Were it not that My believing servant would grieve, I would crown the head of the disbeliever with crowns; he would not be struck with a headache, nor would a vein throb with pain from him."

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah related to us: al-Firyabi related to us: Ibrahim ibn al-'Ala' al-Zubaydi related to us: Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash related to us, from Tha'laba ibn Muslim, from Muslim ibn Abi al-Mujarrad, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to say: "If a man were to flee from his provision, it would pursue him until it overtook him, just as death overtakes one who flees from it. Everyone has a term he will reach, a trace he will tread, a provision he will eat, and a trade by which he will earn. So fear Allah and be graceful in seeking. Let not the delay of some provision lead you to seek it through disobedience to Allah the Exalted, for what is with Him is not attained except through obeying Him, and what is with Him is not reached through disobeying Him. So fear Allah and be graceful in seeking."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 43, verse 36–50:

﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾, meaning: who does not fear His punishment and does not hope for His reward.

Al-Dahhak said: "yamdi qudaman" (he goes forward). Al-Qurazi said: "yuwalli zahrahu 'ala dhikr al-Rahman," (he turns his back on the remembrance of the Most Merciful), which is the Qur'an. Abu 'Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: that is, his eye becomes dim. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: the original meaning of al-'asw (turning away) is looking with weak sight. He recited in its meaning:

"Whenever you come to it, peering toward the light of its fire, you find the best fire there, and the best kindler."

Nawfal ibn Abi 'Aqrab related from Ibn 'Abbas that he recited ﴿wa man ya'sha﴾ with a fatha on the shin, and its meaning is "whoever goes blind." It is said of it: "'ashiya ya'shá 'ashyan" when one becomes blind; a man is "a'sha" and a woman is "'ashwa." From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

"He saw a man absent from the company, of disordered form, blind and sightless."

﴿We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his companion﴾, meaning: We join him to him and give him power over him, so he does not separate from him. ﴿And indeed they [the devils] bar them [the disbelievers] from the way﴾, meaning: the devils bar the disbelievers. ﴿While they think that they are guided﴾. ﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾: the people of Iraq and Ibn Muhaysin read it in the singular, meaning the disbeliever; Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading, while the others read "jā'anā" in the dual form, meaning the disbeliever and his companion.

﴿He will say [the disbeliever to the devil]: "Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts"﴾, that is, the east and the west, and the name of one was replaced by the other, as the poet said:

"We took the horizons of the sky over you, for us are its two moons and the rising stars."

meaning the sun and the moon. The morning and the evening are called "al-'asrat," as Humayd ibn Thawr said:

"The two 'asrs will not delay a day and a night, if they seek to overtake what they aim for."

Another said:

"The Basra of the Azd is ours, and Iraq is ours, and the two Mosuls, and among us are the metropolis and the sacred precinct."

He meant Mosul and al-Jazira. Kufa and Basra are called "al-Basratan," Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) are called "al-'Umarān," and the two grandsons (al-Sibtayn) are called "al-Hasanān." Some of them said: he meant by "the two easts" the east of summer and the east of winter.

This is like His saying: ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ [Surah al-Rahman: 17].

﴿Miserable is the companion﴾. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: when the disbeliever is resurrected, his spouse is with him, along with his devilish companion, and he does not separate from him until he reaches the Fire.

﴿And it will not benefit you today﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿since you did wrong﴾, by associating partners in the world, ﴿that you will be sharing in the punishment﴾, meaning: your associating in the punishment will not benefit you, because each one has his full share of it, so the punishment will not be lightened for you on account of your companions.

Muqatil said: ﴿It will not benefit you today﴾, meaning regret and remorse, ﴿because you and your companions are sharing the punishment today, just as you were sharing in disbelief.﴾

﴿Can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind, and those who are in manifest error?﴾ meaning the disbelievers against whom the word of punishment has been fulfilled, so they do not believe.

﴿So whether We take you away, We will surely take revenge upon them﴾, meaning: We will cause you to die before We punish them. ﴿Or We show you that which We promised them﴾, so that We punish them during your lifetime.

﴿For indeed We have power over them﴾. Most of the exegetes said: it refers to the polytheists of Mecca, and He took revenge upon them on the day of Badr. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: it refers to the people of Islam from the community of Muhammad ﷺ, and after the Prophet of mercy there was severe retribution; Allah honoured His Prophet and took him away, and he did not see in his community except what gladdens his eye, and the retribution remained after him. There is no prophet except that he is shown the punishment within his community.

It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet ﷺ was shown what would befall his community after him, and he was not seen laughing or relaxed until Allah took him.

﴿So hold fast to what has been revealed to you; indeed you are upon a straight path. And indeed it [the Qur'an] is a reminder for you﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and for your people﴾ from Quraysh, ﴿a source of honour for you. And you will be questioned﴾ about its right and the performance of its thanks.

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Abu 'Ali ibn Habash al-Muqri narrated to us: Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Jawhari narrated to us: my uncle narrated to us: Sayf ibn 'Umar al-Kufi narrated to us, from Wa'il Abu Bakr, from al-Zuhayri, from 'Abd Allah and 'Atiyya ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Ayyub, from 'Ali, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to present himself to the tribes in Mecca, promising them victory. When they said, "To whom will the rule belong after you?", he would remain silent and tell them nothing, because he had not been commanded in that matter, until there was revealed: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾. After that, whenever he was asked, he would say: "To Quraysh," but they would not respond to him, and the Ansar accepted him on that basis.

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Nasr ibn Mansur ibn Ja'far al-Nahawandi narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn al-Jarud narrated to us: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: al-Walid narrated to us, from al-'Umari, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This affair will remain with Quraysh as long as two people remain among mankind" [194].

'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Nahid informed us: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed us: al-Hasan ibn Nasih and Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, both saying: Nu'aym ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Hasan ibn Muti', from Mu'awiya, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "This affair will remain with Quraysh; no one opposes them except that Allah overturns him on his face, as long as they uphold the religion" [195].

'Ubayd Allah al-Zahid informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj informed us: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahim narrated to us: Hawdha ibn Khalifa narrated to us: 'Awf narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Mihraq, from Abu Kinana, from Abu Musa, who said: The Prophet ﷺ stood at the door of the House, and in it were some men of Quraysh. He took hold of the two posts of the door and said:

"Is there in the House anyone other than a Qurayshi?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah, except a sister's son of ours." He said: "The sister's son of a people is from them." Then he said: "This affair will remain with Quraysh as long as they, when they judge, act justly; when they are asked for mercy, they show mercy; and when they make a covenant, they fulfil it. Whoever does not do that, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and mankind, all together; Allah will not accept from him any repentance or ransom" [196].

'Ubayd Allah al-Zahid narrated to us, my father al-'Abbas al-Sarraj narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahim narrated to me: Musa ibn Dawud and Khalid ibn Khidash narrated to us, both saying: Bukayr ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, from Yasar ibn Salama, from Abu Burda, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The rulers are from Quraysh. For me upon them is a right, and for them upon you is a right, as long as they do three things: when they judge, they act justly; when they are asked for mercy, they show mercy; and when they make a covenant, they fulfil it" [Musnad Ahmad].

Khalid added: "Whoever does not do that, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and mankind, all together" [197].

Ibn Fanjawayh narrated to us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: I heard Malik ibn Anas say, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾: it is the saying of a man, "My father narrated to me, from my grandfather."

﴿And ask, O Muhammad, those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾

The scholars differed concerning those who were asked. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Hasan and the two Muqatils said: they are the believers of the two Scriptures. They said: it is in the recitation of 'Abd Allah and Ubayy: "Ask those whom We sent to them before you, Our messengers." Ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd said: they are the prophets who were gathered for him on the night of his Night Journey to Bayt al-Maqdis.

Ibn Fanjawayh narrated to us: Musa ibn Muhammad narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiya narrated to us: Isma'il ibn 'Isa narrated to us: al-Musayyab narrated to us, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Dimashqi said: I heard al-Zuhri say: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, every prophet who had been sent prayed behind him that night, and it was said to the Prophet (peace be upon him): ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you﴾.

al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari narrated to us: Abu al-Fath Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Azdi al-Mawsili narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ghazwan al-Baghdadi narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Jabir narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah and Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Suqa, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "An angel came to me and said: 'O Muhammad, ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: upon what were they sent?' I said: 'Upon what were they sent?' He said: 'Upon your guardianship and the guardianship of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib'" [198].

﴿And indeed We sent Musa with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and he said: "I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds." But when he brought them Our signs, behold, they laughed at them, and they mocked and denied them.﴾

﴿And We did not show them any sign except that it was greater than its sister﴾, meaning its counterpart and companion that came before it.

﴿And We seized them with punishment﴾, namely by the years of drought, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, ﴿that perhaps they would return﴾. ﴿And they said, when they witnessed the punishment: "O sorcerer"﴾, meaning: O perfect and skilled scholar. They only said this out of honour and reverence, because sorcery was among them a great knowledge and a praiseworthy attribute. It was also said: the meaning is "O you who overcame us by your sorcery," like the Arab saying: "I disputed with him and overcame him," and similar expressions.

It is possible that they meant by it the sorcerer in the literal sense, as an insult to him, and Musa (peace be upon him) did not object to their address to him in that manner, hoping that they would believe.

meaning the sun and the moon. The morning and the evening are called "al-'asrat," as Humayd ibn Thawr said:

﴿And it will not benefit you today﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿since you did wrong﴾, by associating partners in the world, ﴿that you will be sharing in the punishment﴾, meaning: your associating in the punishment will not benefit you, because each one has his full share of it, so the punishment will not be lightened for you on account of your companions.

Muqatil said: ﴿It will not benefit you today﴾, meaning regret and remorse, ﴿because you and your companions are sharing the punishment today, just as you were sharing in disbelief.﴾

﴿Can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind, and those who are in manifest error?﴾ meaning the disbelievers against whom the word of punishment has been fulfilled, so they do not believe.

﴿So whether We take you away, We will surely take revenge upon them﴾, meaning: We will cause you to die before We punish them. ﴿Or We show you that which We promised them﴾, so that We punish them during your lifetime.

﴿For indeed We have power over them﴾. Most of the exegetes said: it refers to the polytheists of Mecca, and He took revenge upon them on the day of Badr. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: it refers to the people of Islam from the community of Muhammad ﷺ, and after the Prophet of mercy there was severe retribution; Allah honoured His Prophet and took him away, and he did not see in his community except what gladdens his eye, and the retribution remained after him. There is no prophet except that he is shown the punishment within his community.

It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet ﷺ was shown what would befall his community after him, and he was not seen laughing or relaxed until Allah took him.

﴿So hold fast to what has been revealed to you; indeed you are upon a straight path. And indeed it [the Qur'an] is a reminder for you﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and for your people﴾ from Quraysh, ﴿a source of honour for you. And you will be questioned﴾ about its right and the performance of its thanks.

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Abu 'Ali ibn Habash al-Muqri narrated to us: Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Jawhari narrated to us: my uncle narrated to us: Sayf ibn 'Umar al-Kufi narrated to us, from Wa'il Abu Bakr, from al-Zuhayri, from 'Abd Allah and 'Atiyya ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Ayyub, from 'Ali, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to present himself to the tribes in Mecca, promising them victory. When they said, "To whom will the rule belong after you?", he would remain silent and tell them nothing, because he had not been commanded in that matter, until there was revealed: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾. After that, whenever he was asked, he would say: "To Quraysh," but they would not respond to him, and the Ansar accepted him on that basis.

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Nasr ibn Mansur ibn Ja'far al-Nahawandi narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn al-Jarud narrated to us: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: al-Walid narrated to us, from al-'Umari, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This affair will remain with Quraysh as long as two people remain among mankind" [194].

'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Nahid informed us: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed us: al-Hasan ibn Nasih and Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, both saying: Nu'aym ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Hasan ibn Muti', from Mu'awiya, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "This affair will remain with Quraysh; no one opposes them except that Allah overturns him on his face, as long as they uphold the religion" [195].

'Ubayd Allah al-Zahid informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj informed us: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahim narrated to us: Hawdha ibn Khalifa narrated to us: 'Awf narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Mihraq, from Abu Kinana, from Abu Musa, who said: The Prophet ﷺ stood at the door of the House, and in it were some men of Quraysh. He took hold of the two posts of the door and said:

"Is there in the House anyone other than a Qurayshi?" They said: "No, O Messenger of Allah, except a sister's son of ours." He said: "The sister's son of a people is from them." Then he said: "This affair will remain with Quraysh as long as they, when they judge, act justly; when they are asked for mercy, they show mercy; and when they make a covenant, they fulfil it. Whoever does not do that, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and mankind, all together; Allah will not accept from him any repentance or ransom" [196].

'Ubayd Allah al-Zahid narrated to us, my father al-'Abbas al-Sarraj narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahim narrated to me: Musa ibn Dawud and Khalid ibn Khidash narrated to us, both saying: Bukayr ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, from Yasar ibn Salama, from Abu Burda, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The rulers are from Quraysh. For me upon them is a right, and for them upon you is a right, as long as they do three things: when they judge, they act justly; when they are asked for mercy, they show mercy; and when they make a covenant, they fulfil it" [Musnad Ahmad].

Khalid added: "Whoever does not do that, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and mankind, all together" [197].

Ibn Fanjawayh narrated to us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: I heard Malik ibn Anas say, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾: it is the saying of a man, "My father narrated to me, from my grandfather."

﴿And ask, O Muhammad, those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾

The scholars differed concerning those who were asked. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Hasan and the two Muqatils said: they are the believers of the two Scriptures. They said: it is in the recitation of 'Abd Allah and Ubayy: "Ask those whom We sent to them before you, Our messengers." Ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd said: they are the prophets who were gathered for him on the night of his Night Journey to Bayt al-Maqdis.

Ibn Fanjawayh narrated to us: Musa ibn Muhammad narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiya narrated to us: Isma'il ibn 'Isa narrated to us: al-Musayyab narrated to us, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Dimashqi said: I heard al-Zuhri say: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, every prophet who had been sent prayed behind him that night, and it was said to the Prophet (peace be upon him): ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you﴾.

al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari narrated to us: Abu al-Fath Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Azdi al-Mawsili narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ghazwan al-Baghdadi narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Jabir narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah and Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Suqa, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "An angel came to me and said: 'O Muhammad, ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: upon what were they sent?' I said: 'Upon what were they sent?' He said: 'Upon your guardianship and the guardianship of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib'" [198].

﴿And indeed We sent Musa with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and he said: "I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds." But when he brought them Our signs, behold, they laughed at them, and they mocked and denied them.﴾

﴿And We did not show them any sign except that it was greater than its sister﴾, meaning its counterpart and companion that came before it.

﴿And We seized them with punishment﴾, namely by the years of drought, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, ﴿that perhaps they would return﴾. ﴿And they said, when they witnessed the punishment: "O sorcerer"﴾, meaning: O perfect and skilled scholar. They only said this out of honour and reverence, because sorcery was among them a great knowledge and a praiseworthy attribute. It was also said: the meaning is "O you who overcame us by your sorcery," like the Arab saying: "I disputed with him and overcame him," and similar expressions.

It is possible that they meant by it the sorcerer in the literal sense, as an insult to him, and Musa (peace be upon him) did not object to their address to him in that manner, hoping that they would believe.

﴿Pray for us to your Lord by what He has promised you﴾, meaning: by what You have informed us He has covenanted with you, ﴿that we, if we believe, He will remove the punishment from us. Ask Him, then, to remove it from us.﴾ ﴿Indeed we are guided﴾, meaning: believers.

﴿But when We removed the punishment from them, behold, they broke their word﴾, meaning: they violated their covenant, persisted in their disbelief, and disputed in their error.

﴿And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people, saying: "O my people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me?"﴾ That is, the rivers of the Nile, the principal ones of which are four: the Nahr al-Malik, the Nahr Tulun, the Nahr Damyat, and the Nahr Tinnis. ﴿Flowing beneath me﴾ means: before me, among my gardens and orchards. Ibn Abbas said: "around me." Ata said: "in my grip and under my dominion." Al-Hasan said: "by my command."

﴿Do you not see? Or am I better than this one who is despised, and can hardly express himself?﴾ Here "am" (أم) means "rather" (بل), and it is not a conjunction according to the view of most exegetes. Al-Farra' said: some people of the scholars of meaning stop at the word "am" and the sentence is complete there.

There is an implied element in the verse, and its sense is: "Do you not see? Or do you not see? Rather, [Pharaoh] began: 'I am better than this one who is despised,'" meaning Musa (peace be upon him), who is weak and insignificant. ﴿And who can hardly express himself﴾ means he is unable to speak clearly with his argument, because of his stammer, the knot in his tongue, and the impediment in his speech.

﴿Why then have bracelets of gold not been bestowed upon him, or angels not come with him in procession, if he is truthful?﴾ Al-Hasan, Ya'qub, Abu Hatim and Hafs read ﴿asawiratun﴾ as the plural of "siwar" (bracelet). Ubayy read ﴿asawir﴾ (the plural of "iswar," bracelet). Ibn Mas'ud read ﴿asawir﴾ as well. The common readers read ﴿asawiratun﴾ with an alif, as the plural of "aswirah," which is a plural of a plural.

Abu Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: the singular of ﴿asawirah﴾, ﴿asawir﴾ and ﴿asawir﴾ is ﴿asawir﴾, and it is a dialectal form of "siwar." Mujahid said: when they wished to make a man a leader, they would place a bracelet on him and a golden torque around his neck, and that was a sign of his lordship and a mark of his chieftaincy. So Pharaoh said: "Why has the Lord of Musa not cast down upon him bracelets of gold?" (See the tafsir of al-Tabari 25/106, and the tafsir of al-Qurtubi 16/100.)

﴿Or the angels came with him, in procession﴾, meaning following one another, attending him, walking with him as witnesses in his favor. (Tafsir al-Tabari 25/106.)

God Most High said: ﴿So he made light of his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a people who were defiantly disobedient.﴾ That is, he found his people, the Copts, to be ignorant.

We were informed by Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh: Ibn Malik narrated to us: Ibn Hanbal narrated to us: my father narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, who said: al-Dahhak ibn Abd al-Rahim ibn Abi Hawshab said: I heard Bilal ibn Sa'd say: Abu al-Darda' said: "If this world weighed in God's sight the wing of a gnat, Pharaoh would not have been given a drink of it."

﴿So when they angered Us﴾, meaning provoked Us. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: they opposed Us. ﴿We took vengeance upon them and drowned them all﴾, ﴿and We made them a precedent﴾. Ali and Ibn Mas'ud read ﴿salafan﴾ with a damma on the sin and a fatha on the lam. Al-Mu'arrikh and al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: it is the plural of "salfah," like "tarqah" and "turq," and "ghurfah" and "ghurf." Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a damma on the sin and the lam. Al-Farra' said: it is the plural of "salif." It is related from al-Qasim ibn Ma'in that he heard the Arabs say: "A salif of people has passed away." Abu Hatim said: "salaf" and "salaf" are the same, like "khashab" and "khashab," and "thamar" and "thamar." The rest read it with a fatha on the sin and the lam, as the plural of "salif," like "hari's" and "haras," and "rasid" and "rassad." All of them mean: those who have passed and gone before among the nations.

﴿And an example for the later ones﴾: a lesson for whoever comes after them. The exegetes said: a precedent for the disbelievers of this nation, leading them to the Fire.

﴿And when the son of Mary was cited as an example﴾, in respect of his creation without a father. He was compared to Adam, who had neither father nor mother. ﴿Behold, your people turn away from it, shouting in protest﴾, and they say: "Muhammad only wants us to worship him and take him as a god, just as the Christians worshipped Jesus." This was said by Qatadah.

Ibn Abbas said: it refers to the disputation of Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari with the Prophet (ﷺ), and to the matter of Jesus (peace be upon him). We have mentioned it in the chapter of the Prophets (peace be upon them). The readers differed concerning ﴿yasiddun﴾. The people of Medina, the people of Syria, and a group of the Kufans read it with a damma on the sad, and this is the reading of Ali and al-Nakha'i, and its meaning is "they turn away." Its parallel is the saying of God: ﴿You see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 61).

The rest read it with a kasra on the sad, and this is the preference of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim. They differed about its meaning. Al-Kisa'i said: "They are two dialects, like ﴿ya'rishun﴾ and ﴿ya'rushun﴾, and ﴿ya'kufun﴾ and ﴿ya'kifun﴾, and 'darrat al-shah tadirru' and 'tadurru' (the sheep gave milk), and 'shadha 'alayhi yashudhdhu' and 'yashiddu', and 'namma al-hadith yanummuhu' and 'yanimmuhu'." Ibn Abbas said: its meaning is "they cry out." Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: "they shout." Al-Dahhak: "they shriek." Qatadah: "they lament and laugh." Al-Qurazi said: "they are vexed."

Al-Farra' said: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to me that Asim read ﴿yasiddun﴾ from the reading of Abu Abd al-Rahman, and he read ﴿yasuddun﴾. In another report, Ibn Abbas met the brother of Ubayd ibn Umayr and said: "Your uncle is an Arab; why then does he commit a grammatical error in His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Behold, your people turn away from it, shouting in protest﴾?"

﴿And they said: "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾ They mean Muhammad (ﷺ), so that we would worship his god, obey him, and abandon our gods. This is the saying of Qatadah. Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: "or is he?" means Jesus (peace be upon him). They said: "Muhammad claims that everything worshipped besides God is in the Fire, so we are content that our gods be with Ezra, Jesus and the angels in the Fire."

God Most High said: ﴿They did not cite it to you except as a dispute﴾, that is, they cited this example as a mere argument of falsehood. ﴿Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾

We were informed by Abu Bakr Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Ali al-Jamshadhi the jurist, through my reading to him: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn Malik al-Qati'i narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us: my father narrated to me: Abd Allah ibn Numayr al-Kufi narrated to us: Hajjaj ibn Dinar al-Wasiti narrated to us: Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun narrated to us: al-Sarri narrated to us: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us: Anbasah ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Qurashi narrated to us, from Hajjaj ibn Dinar, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umama, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No people have strayed after guidance they were upon, except that they took up disputation." Then he recited: ﴿They did not cite it to you except as a dispute. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾ (Musnad Ahmad 5/256.)

﴿He was only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, meaning a sign or a lesson, an admonition of his for the Children of Israel. ﴿And if We willed, We would have made from among you angels in the earth succeeding one another﴾, meaning We would have destroyed you and made replacements from among you, angels who would be your successors, inhabiting the earth, worshipping Me and obeying Me.

﴿And indeed, it﴾, meaning Jesus (peace be upon him), ﴿is a sign of the Hour﴾, by his descent it is known that the Hour will come, and it is evidence of the passing of this world and the coming of the Hereafter.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Talhah ibn Muhammad and Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bishr ibn Mujahid narrated to us: Fadl ibn al-Hasan narrated to us: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Imran ibn Jarir, who said: "I heard Abu Nadrah recite ﴿And indeed, it is a sign of the Hour﴾," and he said: "It is Jesus." With his chain from Ibn Mujahid: my father narrated to me, Abd Allah ibn [Umar] ibn Sa'd narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Abu Makki narrated to us, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And indeed, it is a sign of the Hour﴾, who said: "That is Jesus (peace be upon him)."

Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, Qatadah, Malik ibn Dinar and al-Dahhak read ﴿wa-innahu la-'alamun lil-sa'ah﴾ with a fatha on the ayn and the lam, meaning a sign and an indication.

In a hadith: Jesus son of Mary will descend at a pass in the Holy Land called Afiq, between two yellowed garments, his hair anointed, and in his hand a spear with which he will slay the Dajjal. He will come to Jerusalem while the people are at the Asr prayer, and the imam will lead them. The imam will step back, and Jesus will advance and pray behind him, upon the law of Muhammad (ﷺ). Then he will kill the swine, break the cross, destroy the churches and synagogues, and kill the Christians, except those who believe in him.

Some people said: the pronoun in ﴿wa-innahu﴾ refers to the Qur'an, and the meaning of the verse is: "And indeed the Qur'an is a sign of the Hour," informing you of its coming and telling you of its circumstances and terrors. Al-Hasan adopted this view.

﴿So do not doubt it﴾, meaning do not be in doubt about it, that is, concerning it. ﴿And follow Me; this is a straight path. And let not Satan prevent you; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ ﴿And when Jesus came to the Children of Israel with clear proofs, he said: "I have come to you with wisdom"﴾, meaning prophethood, ﴿and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ﴾, namely some of the rulings of the Torah.

﴿So fear God and obey me. Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, the Jews and the Christians. ﴿So woe to those who wronged﴾, meaning who disbelieved and associated partners with God, as in Surah Maryam, ﴿from the punishment of a painful day. Do they await but the Hour, that it will come upon them suddenly while they perceive not?﴾ ﴿Close friends, that Day, will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ The close friends in disobedience in this world. ﴿That Day﴾ means the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Except the righteous﴾: those who love one another for God's sake, upon the obedience of God.

We were informed by Aqil ibn Muhammad that Abu al-Hariq al-Baghdadi, the judge, informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Abu Ishaq, that Ali (may God be pleased with him) said concerning this verse: "Two believing friends and two disbelieving friends. When one of the believers dies, he says: 'O Lord, indeed so-and-so used to command me to obey You and Your Messenger, and command me to good, and forbid me from evil, and inform me that I will meet You. O Lord, do not let him go astray after me, guide him as You guided me, and honor him as You honored me.'

When his believing friend dies, He brings them together and says: 'Let each of you praise his companion.' He says: 'O Lord, indeed he used to command me to obey You and Your Messenger, and command me to good and forbid me from evil, and inform me that I will meet You.' He says: 'An excellent brother, an excellent friend, and an excellent companion.'

He said: And one of the two disbelievers dies, and says: 'Indeed so-and-so used to forbid me from obeying You and Your Messenger, and command me to evil, and forbid me from good, and inform me that I will not meet You.'

He says: 'An evil brother, an evil friend, and an evil companion.'"

﴿And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people, saying: "O my people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me?"﴾ That is, the rivers of the Nile, the principal ones of which are four: the Nahr al-Malik, the Nahr Tulun, the Nahr Damyat, and the Nahr Tinnis. ﴿Flowing beneath me﴾ means: before me, among my gardens and orchards. ﴿Or the angels came with him, in procession﴾, meaning following one another, attending him, walking with him as witnesses in his favor. (Tafsir al-Tabari 25/106.)

God Most High said: ﴿They did not cite it to you except as a dispute﴾, that is, they cited this example as a mere argument of falsehood. ﴿Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾

Then he recited: ﴿They did not cite it to you except as a dispute. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾ (Musnad Ahmad 5/256.)

﴿He was only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, meaning a sign or a lesson, an admonition of his for the Children of Israel. ﴿And if We willed, We would have made from among you angels in the earth succeeding one another﴾, meaning We would have destroyed you and made replacements from among you, angels who would be your successors, inhabiting the earth, worshipping Me and obeying Me.

﴿And indeed, it﴾, meaning Jesus (peace be upon him), ﴿is a sign of the Hour﴾, by his descent it is known that the Hour will come, and it is evidence of the passing of this world and the coming of the Hereafter.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Talhah ibn Muhammad and Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bishr ibn Mujahid narrated to us: Fadl ibn al-Hasan narrated to us: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Imran ibn Jarir, who said: "I heard Abu Nadrah recite ﴿And indeed, it is a sign of the Hour﴾," and he said: "It is Jesus." In a hadith: Jesus son of Mary will descend at a pass in the Holy Land called Afiq, between two yellowed garments, his hair anointed, and in his hand a spear with which he will slay the Dajjal. He will come to Jerusalem while the people are at the Asr prayer, and the imam will lead them. The imam will step back, and Jesus will advance and pray behind him, upon the law of Muhammad (ﷺ). Then he will kill the swine, break the cross, destroy the churches and synagogues, and kill the Christians, except those who believe in him.

Some people said: the pronoun in ﴿wa-innahu﴾ refers to the Qur'an, and the meaning of the verse is: "And indeed the Qur'an is a sign of the Hour," informing you of its coming and telling you of its circumstances and terrors. Al-Hasan adopted this view.

﴿So do not doubt it﴾, meaning do not be in doubt about it, that is, concerning it. ﴿And follow Me; this is a straight path. This is a straight path.﴾ ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, the Jews and the Christians. ﴿So woe to those who wronged﴾, meaning who disbelieved and associated partners with God, as in Surah Maryam, ﴿from the punishment of a painful day. When one of the believers dies, he says: 'O Lord, indeed so-and-so used to command me to obey You and Your Messenger, and command me to good, and forbid me from evil, and inform me that I will meet You. When his believing friend dies, He brings them together and says: 'Let each of you praise his companion.' He says: 'O Lord, indeed he used to command me to obey You and Your Messenger, and command me to good and forbid me from evil, and inform me that I will meet You.' He says: 'An excellent brother, an excellent friend, and an excellent companion.'

He said: And one of the two disbelievers dies, and says: 'Indeed so-and-so used to forbid me from obeying You and Your Messenger, and command me to evil, and forbid me from good, and inform me that I will not meet You.'

He says: 'An evil brother, an evil friend, and an evil companion.'"

Al-Farra' said: some people of the scholars of meaning stop at the word "am" and the sentence is complete there.

﴿He was only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, meaning a sign or a lesson, an admonition of his for the Children of Israel. ﴿And if We willed, We would have made from among you angels in the earth succeeding one another﴾, meaning We would have destroyed you and made replacements from among you, angels who would be your successors, inhabiting the earth, worshipping Me and obeying Me.

﴿And indeed, it﴾, meaning Jesus (peace be upon him), ﴿is a sign of the Hour﴾, by his descent it is known that the Hour will come, and it is evidence of the passing of this world and the coming of the Hereafter.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Talhah ibn Muhammad and Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bishr ibn Mujahid narrated to us: Fadl ibn al-Hasan narrated to us: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Imran ibn Jarir, who said: "I heard Abu Nadrah recite ﴿And indeed, it is a sign of the Hour﴾," and he said: "It is Jesus." With his chain from Ibn Mujahid: my father narrated to me, Abd Allah ibn [Umar] ibn Sa'd narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Abu Makki narrated to us, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And indeed, it is a sign of the Hour﴾, who said: "That is Jesus (peace be upon him)."

Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, Qatadah, Malik ibn Dinar and al-Dahhak read ﴿wa-innahu la-'alamun lil-sa'ah﴾ with a fatha on the ayn and the lam, meaning a sign and an indication.

In a hadith: Jesus son of Mary will descend at a pass in the Holy Land called Afiq, between two yellowed garments, his hair anointed, and in his hand a spear with which he will slay the Dajjal. He will come to Jerusalem while the people are at the Asr prayer, and the imam will lead them. The imam will step back, and Jesus will advance and pray behind him, upon the law of Muhammad (ﷺ). Then he will kill the swine, break the cross, destroy the churches and synagogues, and kill the Christians, except those who believe in him.

Some people said: the pronoun in ﴿wa-innahu﴾ refers to the Qur'an, and the meaning of the verse is: "And indeed the Qur'an is a sign of the Hour," informing you of its coming and telling you of its circumstances and terrors. Al-Hasan adopted this view.

﴿So do not doubt it﴾, meaning do not be in doubt about it, that is, concerning it. ﴿And follow Me; this is a straight path. And let not Satan prevent you; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ ﴿And when Jesus came to the Children of Israel with clear proofs, he said: "I have come to you with wisdom"﴾, meaning prophethood, ﴿and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ﴾, namely some of the rulings of the Torah.

﴿So fear God and obey me. Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, the Jews and the Christians. ﴿So woe to those who wronged﴾, meaning who disbelieved and associated partners with God, as in Surah Maryam, ﴿from the punishment of a painful day. Do they await but the Hour, that it will come upon them suddenly while they perceive not?﴾ ﴿Close friends, that Day, will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ The close friends in disobedience in this world. ﴿That Day﴾ means the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Except the righteous﴾: those who love one another for God's sake, upon the obedience of God.

We were informed by Aqil ibn Muhammad that Abu al-Hariq al-Baghdadi, the judge, informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Abu Ishaq, that Ali (may God be pleased with him) said concerning this verse: "Two believing friends and two disbelieving friends. When one of the believers dies, he says: 'O Lord, indeed so-and-so used to command me to obey You and Your Messenger, and command me to good, and forbid me from evil, and inform me that I will meet You. O Lord, do not let him go astray after me, guide him as You guided me, and honor him as You honored me.'

When his believing friend dies, He brings them together and says: 'Let each of you praise his companion.' He says: 'O Lord, indeed he used to command me to obey You and Your Messenger, and command me to good and forbid me from evil, and inform me that I will meet You.' He says: 'An excellent brother, an excellent friend, and an excellent companion.'

He said: And one of the two disbelievers dies, and says: 'Indeed so-and-so used to forbid me from obeying You and Your Messenger, and command me to evil, and forbid me from good, and inform me that I will not meet You.'

He says: 'An evil brother, an evil friend, and an evil companion.'"

﴿And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people, saying: "O my people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me?"﴾ That is, the rivers of the Nile, the principal ones of which are four: the Nahr al-Malik, the Nahr Tulun, the Nahr Damyat, and the Nahr Tinnis. ﴿Flowing beneath me﴾ means: before me, among my gardens and orchards. Ibn Abbas said: "around me." Ata said: "in my grip and under my dominion." Al-Hasan said: "by my command."

﴿Do you not see? Or am I better than this one who is despised, and can hardly express himself?﴾ Here "am" (أم) means "rather" (بل), and it is not a conjunction according to the view of most exegetes. Al-Farra' said: some people of the scholars of meaning stop at the word "am" and the sentence is complete there.

There is an implied element in the verse, and its sense is: "Do you not see? Or do you not see? Rather, [Pharaoh] began: 'I am better than this one who is despised,'" meaning Musa (peace be upon him), who is weak and insignificant. ﴿And who can hardly express himself﴾ means he is unable to speak clearly with his argument, because of his stammer, the knot in his tongue, and the impediment in his speech.

﴿Why then have bracelets of gold not been bestowed upon him, or angels not come with him in procession, if he is truthful?﴾ Al-Hasan, Ya'qub, Abu Hatim and Hafs read ﴿asawiratun﴾ as the plural of "siwar" (bracelet). Ubayy read ﴿asawir﴾ (the plural of "iswar," bracelet). Ibn Mas'ud read ﴿asawir﴾ as well. The common readers read ﴿asawiratun﴾ with an alif, as the plural of "aswirah," which is a plural of a plural.

Abu Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: the singular of ﴿asawirah﴾, ﴿asawir﴾ and ﴿asawir﴾ is ﴿asawir﴾, and it is a dialectal form of "siwar." Mujahid said: when they wished to make a man a leader, they would place a bracelet on him and a golden torque around his neck, and that was a sign of his lordship and a mark of his chieftaincy. So Pharaoh said: "Why has the Lord of Musa not cast down upon him bracelets of gold?" (See the tafsir of al-Tabari 25/106, and the tafsir of al-Qurtubi 16/100.)

﴿Or the angels came with him, in procession﴾, meaning following one another, attending him, walking with him as witnesses in his favor. (Tafsir al-Tabari 25/106.)

God Most High said: ﴿So he made light of his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a people who were defiantly disobedient.﴾ That is, he found his people, the Copts, to be ignorant.

We were informed by Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh: Ibn Malik narrated to us: Ibn Hanbal narrated to us: my father narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, who said: al-Dahhak ibn Abd al-Rahim ibn Abi Hawshab said: I heard Bilal ibn Sa'd say: Abu al-Darda' said: "If this world weighed in God's sight the wing of a gnat, Pharaoh would not have been given a drink of it."

﴿So when they angered Us﴾, meaning provoked Us. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: they opposed Us. ﴿We took vengeance upon them and drowned them all﴾, ﴿and We made them a precedent﴾. Ali and Ibn Mas'ud read ﴿salafan﴾ with a damma on the sin and a fatha on the lam. Al-Mu'arrikh and al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: it is the plural of "salfah," like "tarqah" and "turq," and "ghurfah" and "ghurf." Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a damma on the sin and the lam. Al-Farra' said: it is the plural of "salif." It is related from al-Qasim ibn Ma'in that he heard the Arabs say: "A salif of people has passed away." Abu Hatim said: "salaf" and "salaf" are the same, like "khashab" and "khashab," and "thamar" and "thamar." The rest read it with a fatha on the sin and the lam, as the plural of "salif," like "hari's" and "haras," and "rasid" and "rassad." All of them mean: those who have passed and gone before among the nations.

﴿And an example for the later ones﴾: a lesson for whoever comes after them. The exegetes said: a precedent for the disbelievers of this nation, leading them to the Fire.

﴿And when the son of Mary was cited as an example﴾, in respect of his creation without a father. He was compared to Adam, who had neither father nor mother. ﴿Behold, your people turn away from it, shouting in protest﴾, and they say: "Muhammad only wants us to worship him and take him as a god, just as the Christians worshipped Jesus." This was said by Qatadah.

Ibn Abbas said: it refers to the disputation of Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari with the Prophet (ﷺ), and to the matter of Jesus (peace be upon him). We have mentioned it in the chapter of the Prophets (peace be upon them). The readers differed concerning ﴿yasiddun﴾. The people of Medina, the people of Syria, and a group of the Kufans read it with a damma on the sad, and this is the reading of Ali and al-Nakha'i, and its meaning is "they turn away." Its parallel is the saying of God: ﴿You see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 61).

The rest read it with a kasra on the sad, and this is the preference of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim. They differed about its meaning. Al-Kisa'i said: "They are two dialects, like ﴿ya'rishun﴾ and ﴿ya'rushun﴾, and ﴿ya'kufun﴾ and ﴿ya'kifun﴾, and 'darrat al-shah tadirru' and 'tadurru' (the sheep gave milk), and 'shadha 'alayhi yashudhdhu' and 'yashiddu', and 'namma al-hadith yanummuhu' and 'yanimmuhu'." Ibn Abbas said: its meaning is "they cry out." Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: "they shout." Al-Dahhak: "they shriek." Qatadah: "they lament and laugh." Al-Qurazi said: "they are vexed."

Al-Farra' said: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to me that Asim read ﴿yasiddun﴾ from the reading of Abu Abd al-Rahman, and he read ﴿yasuddun﴾. In another report, Ibn Abbas met the brother of Ubayd ibn Umayr and said: "Your uncle is an Arab; why then does he commit a grammatical error in His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Behold, your people turn away from it, shouting in protest﴾?"

﴿And they said: "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾ They mean Muhammad (ﷺ), so that we would worship his god, obey him, and abandon our gods. This is the saying of Qatadah. Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: "or is he?" means Jesus (peace be upon him). They said: "Muhammad claims that everything worshipped besides God is in the Fire, so we are content that our gods be with Ezra, Jesus and the angels in the Fire."

God Most High said: ﴿They did not cite it to you except as a dispute﴾, that is, they cited this example as a mere argument of falsehood. ﴿Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.﴾

He says: 'O Lord, indeed he used to command me to obey You and Your Messenger, and command me to good and forbid me from evil, and inform me that I will meet You.' He says: 'An excellent brother, an excellent friend, and an excellent companion.'

He said: And one of the two disbelievers dies, and says: 'Indeed so-and-so used to forbid me from obeying You and Your Messenger, and command me to evil, and forbid me from good, and inform me that I will not meet You.'

He says: 'An evil brother, an evil friend, and an evil companion.'"

Al-Farra' said: some people of the scholars of meaning stop at the word "am" and the sentence is complete there.

The rest read it with a fatha on the sin and the lam, as the plural of "salif," like "hari's" and "haras," and "rasid" and "rassad."
